appearance.identity: Restored pale cylindrical summit shelter, eight viewing windows, dark conical cap, raised closed doorway, readable plaque, cut 1895 flag and three Y anchors.
appearance.epoch: 2025 heritage-authority conservation photographs; 2018 restoration retained original location and rotation.
appearance.master: Original 23236-triangle detailed source master retained byte-for-byte.
appearance.browser: Skyline keeps the small shelter silhouette and anchor cables; district retains real recessed windows and simplified plaque/flag; street retains the readable plaque, cut stencil flag, all rivets and fittings with fewer regular shell/roof subdivisions; closeup is the complete original.
appearance.exclusions: Visitor interior, copied historical panorama, exact summit rock, fabrication dimensions and exact doorway compass bearing.

limitations: Approximate facing and summit fit from the inspected picture and standard viewer PMTiles; no bespoke bearing or exact rock survey. The circular mapped outline fixes location and diameter but cannot establish entrance bearing.
Original detailed master/hash/recipe preserved; small fittings and closed-door presentation are photographic reconstruction.
Shared painted-metal graph plus local pane/shadow colors; no embedded image. Natural rock and surrounding mountain are host terrain.
Four budgeted browser levels retained; interiors/collision and physical-device timings excluded. Footprint replacement remains off.

geographic.groundContactBasis: The inspected exterior picture supports the pale cylindrical shelter, dark conical roof, raised doorway, plaque, cut1895 flag and metal anchors/guy ropes. Standard viewer PMTiles provide the summit working datum 2777.579296317931m. The small original shell/anchor contact plane uses modelY0; coarse summit slope and actual rock details are approximate.
